You said:

GitHub So in the jarbis repo, I need you access the feature/sonarqube branch and see why when I create an order using my container the order doesn't go through even tho an asset exist

ChatGPT said:

I checked feature/sonarqube2—feature/sonarqube doesn’t currently exist—and found several issues that explain this.

The main container issue is missing Kafka. Creating an order saves it as PENDING, then publishes an event to Kafka for settlement. But:

  • docker-compose.yml starts only PostgreSQL and the backend.
  • application.properties points Kafka to localhost:9092. Inside the backend container, that means the backend container itself.

Consequently, an existing asset can pass validation while the order never reaches settlement. The fix is to provide Kafka and set SPRING_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS to its address reachable from the backend container, with matching Kafka advertised listeners.

I also found these problems:

IssueEffect / fix
Application listens on 8081, but Compose maps 8081:8080Requests and health checks target the wrong container port. Set SERVER_PORT: 8080 in the backend environment.
Automatic settlement requires a matching opposite orderAn asset existing alone doesn’t fill a BUY. It needs a SELL for the same asset with sell price ≤ buy price, plus sufficient buyer balance and seller holdings.
Container uses jarbis_db, local configuration uses jarbisAn asset in your local database may not exist in the container database. The request needs the numeric assets.id from the container database.
Controller returns the Order entity directlyOrder.account → Account.orders → Order creates a JSON recursion risk. Return the existing OrderResponseDto instead.

The missing Kafka setup is confirmed in the code; I haven’t verified your running container’s exact failure. Send the order request JSON, its response/error, and the output of:

Bash
docker compose logs --tail=100 jarbis-backend

That will distinguish a failed request from an order that was saved but remains PENDING.

You said:

pull the current status of development and see how the kafka works and can you based on that create a sequence diagram that outlines the kafka flow of events

ChatGPT said:

I checked current development at commit f068d2c. Kafka carries the order ID to the settlement listener after the order is committed. Publishing and consuming happen in the same backend application.

The backend connects to kafka:19092. Compose creates orders.submitted with one partition before starting the backend.

Two details matter:

  • 201 Created means the order was created, not filled. It can remain pending until a matching opposite order arrives.
  • Kafka sending is asynchronous; the publisher doesn’t check its result. Database commit and event delivery aren’t atomic.

Latest response


JARBiS authentication sequence

Based on development at f068d2c, inspected October 8, 2026. This is a code-based diagram, not a runtime trace.

Authentication is implemented inside the backend using AuthController, UserService, JwtService, JwtAuthenticationFilter and SecurityConfig. There is no separate AuthService class or Kafka auth event in this flow.

Signup and login

JWT validation and current-user lookup

Implementation notes

  • POST /auth/register and POST /auth/login are public and skipped by the JWT filter. Registration returns 201; login returns 200. Both successful responses contain a user DTO and a JWT.
  • PasswordEncoder is BCryptPasswordEncoder. Registration stores a password hash; login uses matches against that hash.
  • The token subject is the numeric user ID as a string. Other claims are email, fullName, issued-at and expiration. JwtService signs with an HMAC key derived from the configured secret. The configured expiry is 3,600,000 ms (one hour).
  • SecurityConfig uses stateless sessions. Requests must send Authorization: Bearer <token> to authenticate through this filter.
  • The filter verifies the signed token locally and sets a Long user ID as the SecurityContext principal. It also sets userId, email and fullName request attributes. Token validation itself performs no database lookup.
  • GET /auth/me reads that principal, loads the current user from the database and returns UserResponseDto.
  • For an invalid or expired token, the filter logs the exception and continues the chain without establishing JWT authentication. SecurityConfig requires authentication for protected endpoints. No explicit custom authentication entry point specifies a 401 response for this case, so the diagram deliberately avoids assigning an exact rejection status. This differs from failed login, which explicitly returns 401.
  • /users/, /orders/, /accounts/, /holdings/ and /transactions/** require authentication, as do other endpoints except the configured public routes. Authenticated access alone does not establish resource ownership.
  • The current auth files contain no refresh-token or logout endpoint. There is no token-revocation lookup during parsing.

Code references

  • AuthController.java
  • UserService.java
  • JwtService.java
  • JwtAuthenticationFilter.java
  • SecurityConfig.java
  • GlobalExceptionHandler.java
